detail.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of LICENSE.txt.
- [x] I ran the scoped pre-commit checks and committed formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable AGENTS.md hard rules.
- [x] Required category, area and origin labels are applied.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: SM100 packed D128 split-KV SDPA.

## Summary

Packed split attention writes FP32 partials directly to its workspace, so its output no longer shares the Q staging slab. Enable the existing early-Q handoff for SM100 D128 FP16/BF16 ragged and paged split attention. Release Q after the last QK multiply and overlap the next Q load with the current output tail.

Enable the existing exp2/FMA softmax implementation for that same D128 packed-partial form. Both choices are fixed when the plan compiles.

## Why

The previous THD gate retained the staged-output handshake even though split attention bypasses the staging slab. The existing MMA-owned Q-empty handoff already protects Q reuse; the correction role releases O only after its TMEM reads complete. Scheduler credits and the empty-work protocol are preserved.

The exp2/FMA implementation moves part of softmax exponentiation off the MUFU pipe. Its existing sliding-window and quadrant-softmax exclusions remain. D192 was evaluated separately and is not enabled: its benefit was inconsistent and its extra compilation work was less attractive.

This is a warm kernel optimization. The polynomial softmax form can add cold compilation work; this PR does not claim a cold-plan or serving-throughput improvement.

## Related issues

Follow-up to the existing packed split-KV pipeline. Independent of #1715's combine prefetch; neither PR depends on the other.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API, tuning knob, capability, dependency floor, workspace size, native-binder work or per-run preparation is added. Unsplit THD keeps its staged output store. Dense paths and other architectures retain their existing choices. FP32 partial Stats and final O/LSE contracts are unchanged.

## Testing

Scoped pre-commit passed on all four changed files.

- `pytest -q -m L0 sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_decode_d128_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sm100_exp2_split_arch_gate.py`: 148 passed on SM100.
- `pytest -q -m L0 -k 'test_native_paged_thd_capture_and_rebind and d128_split' sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_prepared_thd.py`: 16 passed on SM100 and 16 passed on SM107. Four explicit split/mask parameters were added to the existing test, covering FP16/BF16, HND/NHD, unmasked/causal/sliding-window attention, pointer rebinding and retained capture.
- CuTe DSL 4.7.0 with quack imported first: 13 existing standalone/prepared test entrypoint calls passed, verifying 11 actual changed kernel owners. These are direct contract calls, not a full pytest run.
- Private delayed-role qualification: separately delayed correction and softmax, forced one persistent CTA, and passed four mixed-length B33/B65 cases / 12 owners for each delay. No production debug knob was added.
- SM103 smoke compilation passed for FP16/BF16 and ragged/paged packed split lowerings with the existing architecture gates off. This is compilation evidence, not execution on an SM103 GPU.

No heuristic winner, candidate ordering or timing threshold is asserted. B200 target qualification used a fresh native build: four interleaved baseline/candidate phases completed 340 full FP64 O/LSE and poisoned-replay checks, with 20 explicit domain/workspace declines. The 13 direct contracts and all 16 added pytest cases also passed on that target. Quantitative performance qualification is tracked separately; the result does not establish a gain for every nondefault configuration or for serving. Host timing varied slightly between runs, and no host-speedup claim is made.

@@ -552,7 +552,8 @@ def _quant_kind(fp8: bool, pertensor: bool) -> str:
 # FMA pipe takes a quarter of every row's exp2 columns.  MEASURED on B200 (same-node A/B/A/B, kernel time, gpt-oss d64 full attention with a sink,
 # all four tp shards): -8..-9 % from 8 sequences x 32K keys up (b=128 x 128K keys 919 -> 841 us at tp8), -3..-6 % at 2K keys, 0 at b=1 x 2K; S_q = 4
 # -4..-5 %.  The kernel folds the split out of the sliding-window builds (a unit there is one or two KV tiles: +2..+5 % at S_q >= 2).  The d128 decode
-# tile is not listed (it is HBM-bound where it is measured); the d64 prefill tile stays off (unmeasured).
+# tile keeps the dense path off (HBM-bound where measured). Its THD split form separately uses the existing f16/d128 flag with a kernel-local
+# packed-partials gate; the d64 prefill tile stays off (unmeasured).
 _EXP2_FMA_SPLIT_DECODE_KERNELS: frozenset[tuple[str, tuple[int, int]]] = frozenset({("f16", (64, 64))})
 
 
@@ -3485,8 +3486,10 @@ def _d64_decode_quad(self) -> bool:
 
     def _decode_early_q(self, params) -> bool:
         """Whether the decode tile (sm100/decode_d128_f16.py: the d64 decode tile, the d128 cga1 tile) takes its early-Q form (``TemplateParams.early_q``)
-        on this build: the measured cc, and a dense / paged plan -- the THD legs keep the staged O store their per-batch runtime descriptors place."""
-        if tuple(self._device_cc) not in _EARLY_Q_CC or self.thd or self._fp8:
+        on this build. Unsplit THD keeps its staged O store; split THD writes FP32 partials directly and leaves the Q slab free."""
+        if tuple(self._device_cc) not in _EARLY_Q_CC or self._fp8:
+            return False
+        if self.thd and not (tuple(self._device_cc) == (10, 0) and tuple(self.flavor) == _SM100_DECODE_FLAVOR and params.cta_mma == 1 and params.split_kv > 1):
             return False
         return bool(params.decode_tile) or (tuple(self.flavor) == _SM100_DECODE_FLAVOR and params.cta_mma == 1)

@@ -272,9 +272,9 @@
 # handshake), so the TMA-LDG warp loads the NEXT tile's Q while this tile is still in its tail -- a tile of one or two KV steps (a sliding window,
 # a short cache at batch) no longer pays the O drain + alias round trip + Q load latency in series.  It needs O out of the slab: the fp32 split
 # partials already go straight from TMEM to the workspace, and the dense / paged half output is stored directly by the correction warps
-# (DIRECT_O).  The THD legs keep the staged TMA store: their per-batch runtime descriptors place the rows.  ``PARAMS.early_q`` (the adapter's claim of
-# the measured cc) gates it: a part nobody measured keeps the staged store.
-EARLY_Q = bool(PARAMS.early_q) and (not CFG.THD_VARLEN) and (not RAGGED_Q)
+# (DIRECT_O). Unsplit THD keeps the staged TMA store; split THD writes FP32 partials directly, so it can release Q after the final BMM1 too.
+# ``PARAMS.early_q`` (the adapter's claim of the measured cc) gates it: a part nobody measured keeps the staged store.
+EARLY_Q = bool(PARAMS.early_q) and (not CFG.THD_VARLEN or _FP32_PARTIALS) and (not RAGGED_Q)
 DIRECT_O = EARLY_Q and not _FP32_PARTIALS
 # Quadrant-cooperative softmax (``PARAMS.decode_quad``, the d64 flavor).  A decode step has at most QUAD_ROWS = 32 live Q rows (S_q x PACK_G), a quarter
 # of the tile's 128 TMEM lanes, yet each of the four softmax warps -- one per lane quadrant -- exponentiates all 128 key columns of its 32 lanes, so the
@@ -295,14 +295,19 @@
 # exp2 split MUFU / FMA (``_E2E_*``), the d128 prefill kernel's pattern (sm100/prefill_d128_f16.py): of every _E2E_FREQ P columns the LAST _E2E_RES are
 # evaluated on the FMA pipe (``exp2_emul_pair``), the rest on MUFU.EX2.  On cc 10.0 the d64 tile's one softmax warpgroup is MUFU-bound at a long KV (16
 # EX2 per clk per SM, and the 128 rows of a tile exponentiate whether live or not), so the FMA pipe takes a quarter of every row's columns.  Gate:
-# ``PARAMS.exp2_fma_split`` (api_dsl._exp2_fma_split_for: cc 10.0 x the d64 decode tile) and ``PARAMS.decode_tile`` (the d64 flavor of this file), and not on
-# a sliding-window build (its units are one or two KV tiles: a latency chain the polynomial's dependent FMAs lengthen, with no MUFU-bound loop to relieve);
+# ``PARAMS.exp2_fma_split`` supplies the measured cc gate. This tile enables it for d64 decode and the measured d128 THD FP32-partial form;
+# d192 THD remains all-MUFU because the split mix did not show a consistent benefit. Do not enable it on a sliding-window build (its units are one or two KV tiles: a latency chain the polynomial's dependent FMAs lengthen, with no MUFU-bound loop to relieve);
 # off, both exp2 sites trace the plain MUFU spelling and the module is IR-identical to the unsplit kernel.  The quadrant softmax (QUAD) leaves it off:
 # a warp exponentiates a quarter of the columns, so the MUFU pipe is no longer the bound.
 _E2E_FREQ = 16
 _E2E_RES = 4
 _E2E_CHUNK = 64  # tcgen05_ld width of one softmax chunk (see _softmax_kv_body CHUNK)
-_E2E_ENABLED = bool(PARAMS.exp2_fma_split) and bool(PARAMS.decode_tile) and (CFG.MASK_FLAGS & MASK_SWA) == 0 and not QUAD
+_E2E_ENABLED = (
+    bool(PARAMS.exp2_fma_split)
+    and (bool(PARAMS.decode_tile) or (CFG.THD_VARLEN and _FP32_PARTIALS and CFG.TILE_K == 128 and CFG.TILE_O == 128))
+    and (CFG.MASK_FLAGS & MASK_SWA) == 0
+    and not QUAD
+)

     """Early Q (``TemplateParams.early_q``) is a positive per-arch claim like the exp2 split: cc 10.0 / 10.3 take it on the decode tile (the d64 decode tile
-    and the d128 cga1 tile), cc 10.7 -- which loads the same tile -- and every unmeasured part keep the staged TMA store, as do THD and FP8 plans."""
+    and the d128 cga1 tile), cc 10.7 -- which loads the same tile -- and every unmeasured part keep the staged TMA store, as do unsplit THD and FP8 plans."""
     from types import SimpleNamespace
 
     from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.api_dsl import SdpaFwdDslSm100

-        return SdpaFwdDslSm100._decode_early_q(me, SimpleNamespace(decode_tile=decode_tile, cta_mma=cta_mma))
+        return SdpaFwdDslSm100._decode_early_q(me, SimpleNamespace(decode_tile=decode_tile, cta_mma=cta_mma, split_kv=1))
 
     assert early_q((10, 0)) and early_q((10, 3)) and early_q((10, 0), flavor=(64, 64), decode_tile=True)
     assert not early_q((10, 7)) and not early_q((11, 0)) and not early_q((12, 0))
